claim.pdf_says:
b) if that operand is a data-name or an identifier, it shall reference one of the following:
    1. an integer intrinsic function,
    2. a fixed-point numeric data item, ...
claim.markdown_says:
b) if that operand is a data-name or an identifier, it shall reference one of the following:

   1\. an integer intrinsic function,

   2\. a fixed-point numeric data item, other than an intrinsic function, ...
claim.why_it_matters: Items 1. and 2. are indented under b) in the PDF as its sub-items; the markdown places them at the same level as a) and b), detaching them from their parent.

verdict.reasoning: Printed page 27 (PDF p51), 5.5 rule 2) b): items '1. an integer intrinsic function,' and '2. a fixed-point numeric data item, other than an intrinsic function, whose description does not include any digit positions to the right of the radix point.' are printed one indent level deeper than a)/b). In page-51.md lines 25-29, the same two items follow b) directly, with every word present and in order. They are indented 3 spaces, the same depth as a) and b), and the escaped '1\.' makes each one a plain paragraph. The only difference is indentation depth. Nothing is missing, moved or misquoted. b) ends with 'one of the following:' and the next sibling is 3), so items 1 and 2 can only belong to b). The rule means the same thing in both sources. This is a formatting difference, not a content discrepancy.
